businessType: Executive search and staffing firm specializing in financial services and tech hiring. Founded 2008, 150 employees (120 recruiters, 30 support), 45 offices across major US markets. Placed 800+ professionals in 2024.
stage: Growth stage: $45M revenue (15% YoY growth, slowing from 25% growth two years ago), EBITDA $6.8M (15% margin, down from 18% two years ago), utilization 78% (down from 82% two years ago). Recruiter productivity declining: revenue per recruiter $300k (down from $340k two years ago). Margin pressure from rising recruiter salaries (+18% in last 18 months).
ownerGoal: Return to 20%+ EBITDA margin and demonstrate profitability leverage within 18 months to support Series B fund-raising or strategic acquisition.
ownerConstraints: Talent market: Recruiting market highly competitive for top talent. Recruiter turnover 20% annually (vs. 12% two years ago); rising retention costs. Offers market competitive but margin-constrained.

Utilization and productivity: Utilization 78% (declining from 82%) suggests bench time increasing or client work declining. Productivity per recruiter declining. Difficult to scale profitably without addressing utilization.
Competitive pressure: Tech and fintech companies hiring directly (not through recruiters), reducing recruiter-dependent hiring. Reduced demand for high-end executive search in certain verticals.
Economic sensitivity: Tech hiring (major segment) sensitive to economic cycles. Current macro uncertainty is impacting hiring budgets.
Scale economics: $45M revenue is below scale-efficient size for profitability; competitor consolidation creating larger, more efficient players.
immediateConcern: Growth stalling (15% current vs. 25% two years ago) while margins compressing (15% current vs. 18%). Recruiter productivity declining (revenue per recruiter down 12% in two years), suggesting either client demand softening or recruiter efficiency declining. Salary costs rising 18% while revenue per recruiter falling, creating a profitability squeeze. Must determine whether problem is demand-driven (fewer placements), supply-driven (recruiter productivity), or structural (market shift away from recruiting firm model).
